key_insight: For geometry-aware hemodynamic surrogates, active learning and physical consistency constraints are more effective during fine-tuning than during early or full-course training.
engineering_relevance: The workflow supports scalable prediction of patient-specific aortic velocity and pressure fields toward real-time cardiovascular flow assessment.
method: Generate synthetic aortic CFD solutions with automatically adjusted, physiologically consistent boundary conditions.
Encode anatomies as displacement fields from a common reference and predict peak-systolic flow using Graph U-Net and Transformer U-Net models.
Improve fine-tuning with gradient- and subspace-based active learning and differentiable finite element residual constraints.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on a SynthAorta-based CFD dataset and out-of-distribution geometries show regime-dependent fine-tuning benefits, but the abstract reports no numerical accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Generalization is primarily limited by the geometric coverage of the anatomy parametrization, rather than by the tested network architectures.
paper_title: Synthetic Dataset Generation, Physical Consistency and Active Learning for Shape-Informed Surrogate Modeling of Hemodynamics
